Put the tank's center at $y=0$; the top of the tank is $y=1$ and the spout outlet is $y=2$. Half full means oil fills $-1\le y\le0$. A slice at height $y$ has area $\pi(1-y^2)$, weighs $60\pi(1-y^2)\,dy$ lb, and is lifted $2-y$ ft:
\[W=\int_{-1}^060\pi(1-y^2)(2-y)\,dy=60\pi\Big[2y-\frac{y^2}{2}-\frac{2y^3}{3}+\frac{y^4}{4}\Big]_{-1}^0=60\pi\cdot\frac{19}{12}=\boxed{95\pi\approx298.5\ \text{ft-lb}}.\]

8:
$y^2-3y+2=(y-1)(y-2)$. Separate with partial fractions $\frac{1}{(y-1)(y-2)}=\frac{1}{y-2}-\frac{1}{y-1}$:
\[\ln\Big|\frac{y-2}{y-1}\Big|=\sin x+C.\]
$y(0)=3$: $C=\ln\frac12$. Near $y=3$ the ratio is positive, so $\frac{y-2}{y-1}=\frac12e^{\sin x}$. Solve for $y$:
\[\boxed{y=\frac{4-e^{\sin x}}{2-e^{\sin x}}}\quad(\text{check: }y(0)=\tfrac{3}{1}=3).\]

\textbf{(a)} $y=10e^{-\alpha t}$ and $8=10e^{-3\alpha}$, so $\alpha=\frac{\ln(5/4)}{3}\approx0.07438$. Then $2=10e^{-\alpha t}$ gives
\[t=\frac{\ln5}{\alpha}=\frac{3\ln5}{\ln1.25}\approx\boxed{21.64\ \text{days}}.\]
\textbf{(b)} $y'=-\alpha y-0.5$ has equilibrium $-\frac{0.5}{\alpha}$, so $y=-\frac{0.5}{\alpha}+\Big(12+\frac{0.5}{\alpha}\Big)e^{-\alpha t}$. With $c=\frac{0.5}{\alpha}\approx6.722$, set $y=2$:
\[e^{-\alpha t}=\frac{2+c}{12+c}\ \Rightarrow\ t=\frac{1}{\alpha}\ln\frac{12+c}{2+c}\approx\boxed{10.27\ \text{days}}.\]
